headline: Israel's Central Elections Committee certifies Oct 27 election results, finds no irregularities'
dek: The Central Elections Committee reviewed complaints from parties, lists and the public, examined protocols from 9,069 polling stations, and found no evidence of irregularities affecting the integrity or outcome of the Oct 27 election; results submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Nov 4, who…
sources: Israel Central Elections Committee statement (acting director Dean Livne; chair Justice Noam Sohlberg)
fault_line: Should the 19 Arab-list seats — their best-ever result — decide who governs Israel, or be treated as illegitimate?

sections.what_happened: The Central Elections Committee reviewed complaints from parties, lists and the public, examined protocols from 9,069 polling stations, and found no evidence of irregularities affecting the integrity or outcome of the Oct 27 election; results submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Nov 4, who begins consultations with party leaders Nov 4-5 and will then task a candidate with forming a government. Final seat split: Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot-led opposition 48, Arab lists 19 of 120; 61 needed for a majority. Likud and Shas representatives abstained on ratification; a separate Shin Bet foreign-interference investigation continues.
sections.what_verified: AP wire, Al Jazeera liveblog, Times of Israel liveblog — three distinct publisher families
sections.what_disputed: Likud and outgoing coalition parties sought to delay certification pending Shin Bet/Mossad/police intelligence on alleged irregularities; committee chair Sohlberg ruled it has no authority to delay certification on investigation grounds. Netanyahu's fraud claims about Arab parties remain unsubstantiated by the committee's review.
sections.why_matters: The fraud challenge failed; the kingmaker math now decides whether Netanyahu survives — watch Herzog's mandate pick, not the certification itself.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog 09:15 GMT = 13:15 ; AP via The Week; Times of Israel): Israel's Central Elections Committee certifies Oct 27 election results, finds no irregularities; Herzog begins government-formation consultations

totw_analysis: Our read: The fraud challenge failed; the kingmaker math now decides whether Netanyahu survives — watch Herzog's mandate pick, not the certification itself. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should the 19 Arab-list seats — their best-ever result — decide who governs Israel, or be treated as illegitimate?
